description: The top of the figure shows the array, indices, and memory addresses, with the column for index 3 highlighted. Below are the address formula and a worked example. Each element occupies 4 bytes. The address row uses two digits (such as 00 and 12), while the calculation uses three (000 and 012). All addresses are decimal. Leading zeros only align the digits.

frames.explanation: Element address = address of first element + element size × index. Indices start at 0, so index 3 identifies the fourth element, whose value is 5. It is three element widths from the start, giving a byte offset of 4 × 3 = 12 and an address of 000 + 4 × 3 = 012. This locates an element by index rather than searching for the value 3.
frames.title: Calculating an array element's address

result: When elements occupy contiguous memory and have equal size, one multiplication and one addition give the address, enabling O(1) random access.
summary: Calculate an element's location directly from the base address, fixed element size, and index.
